name: Sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Both components are cleared by the kidneys. The US label uses the usual regimen above creatinine clearance (CrCl) 30 mL/min, half the usual regimen at 15–30, and does not recommend use below 15. Trimethoprim can cause hyperkalemia (worse with ACE inhibitors, ARBs or kidney impairment) and raises serum creatinine by blocking tubular secretion; crystalluria and interstitial nephritis also occur.

bands.recommendation: Usual regimen (label: CrCl above 30). Keep the patient well hydrated.
Usual regimen at CrCl above 30 (label). Hyperkalemia risk rises in kidney impairment: check potassium, especially with ACE inhibitors, ARBs or spironolactone.
Half the usual regimen at CrCl 15–30 (label). Monitor potassium and creatinine.
Use not recommended at CrCl below 15 mL/min (label table).

hd.text: Label: not recommended below CrCl 15 and gives no dialysis dose; hemodialysis is only moderately effective at removing both components. Use in dialysis (e.g., Pneumocystis prophylaxis) is a specialist decision.

pd.text: Not recommended below CrCl 15 (label); peritoneal dialysis does not remove it. Specialist decision.

crrt.text: Li 2020 (CRRT review, Table 3): trimethoprim 10 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours may be a reasonable starting dose in CVVH or CVVHD (ultrafiltration or dialysate 1–6 L/h); no dose recommended for CVVHDF because of variable sulfamethoxazole clearance.

dialyzable: Moderately by hemodialysis; peritoneal dialysis is not effective (label 10). Both removed by CVVHDF (Li 2020).
monitoring: Potassium (hyperkalemia), creatinine (a rise may reflect blocked tubular secretion of creatinine as well as injury), complete blood count, urinalysis for crystalluria; fluid intake. Sodium (hyponatremia).

pediatric.approved_ages: 2 months and older; contraindicated under 2 months (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: UTI and otitis media: sulfamethoxazole 40 mg/kg and trimethoprim 8 mg/kg per 24 hours in 2 doses. Pneumocystis treatment: sulfamethoxazole 75 to 100 mg/kg and trimethoprim 15 to 20 mg/kg per 24 hours in 4 doses. Pneumocystis prophylaxis: 750/150 mg/m2/day in 2 doses on 3 consecutive days per week (label).
pediatric.max_dose: Prophylaxis: no more than sulfamethoxazole 1,600 mg and trimethoprim 320 mg per day (label).

renal.recommendation: Usual dose at CrCl above 30 (label kidney table is not age-limited). Check potassium.
Half the usual regimen at CrCl 15–30 (label).

crrt.text: No pediatric CRRT data in the cited sources. Specialist input.

adult: JUDGMENT: HD/PD tiles red per label ('use not recommended' below 15). Many units give TMP-SMX after dialysis for Pneumocystis prophylaxis in transplant or glomerulonephritis; Dr. Rivero may prefer amber with a specialist-set dose, but no PubMed-verified dialysis dose has been read for this batch.
Li 2020 CRRT dose was derived for a specific pathogen target (text truncated in PMC; organism not shown) and refers to trimethoprim only.
'Creatinine rise from blocked tubular secretion' is general pharmacology; the label lists 'BUN and serum creatinine elevation' and OCT2 inhibition. Keep or drop?
PH: 400/80 mg (480 mg) and 800/160 mg (960 mg) tablets and 200/40 per 5 mL suspension match US.
